tool_input.command:
cp resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx /tmp/Register.tsx.bak
sed -i '' 's/register\.store/register.stor/' resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx
echo "=== typecheck with wrong route name (expect failure) ===" 
bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -20
cp /tmp/Register.tsx.bak resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx

result: I attached the `RegisterSchema` to the `register.store` route (`routes/auth.ts`) so codegen extracts its body type, regenerated `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, and rewrote `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` to derive its form-data type from `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` and submit via `route('register.store')` instead of a hand-typed shape and a hard-coded `/register` path — matching the pattern already used by the posts/profile forms, including reading validation errors off `form.errors` (Inertia's built-in error tracking) rather than a manually-typed `errors` prop. I confirmed the two required guarantees hold (a misspelled `register.stor` route name and a renamed `passwordConfirmatoin` field both break `bun run typecheck`, even though they're consistent across the single front-end file) and then restored the correct file. I also added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covering the show page, a successful sign-up redirecting to `/dashboard`, and 422s for mismatched confirmation, blank name, and bad email. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (7/7 passing), and `bunx guren check` are all clean.
